title: Foundation: decision backends with typed answers, replay, and scripted modes
body:
## Goal

One small interface that every notebook calls, so a recipe runs offline from fixtures and live against Jev with the same question definitions.

## Scope

- Question definitions for `Choice`, `Noul`, and `Score` that mirror the TypeSafe request shape: `instructions`, and `criteria` as a mapping for Choice or an ordered list for Score. Read S02 and the SDK reference before designing these.
- Typed answer objects that mirror the response shape: Choice has `choice`, `probabilities`, `confidence`; Score has `score`, `probabilities`, `confidence`, `legend`; Noul has `noul` only.
- A `Backend` protocol with one call taking `state` and a mapping of named questions, returning named answers plus `model` and `usage`.
- `ReplayBackend`: answers from recorded fixtures keyed by a stable hash of state and questions. A miss raises an error that names the missing key. It never fabricates an answer.
- `ScriptedBackend`: a deterministic, seeded stand-in driven by a function, for closed-loop recipes where the next request depends on earlier answers. Its answers are always marked synthetic.
- `get_backend()` that returns the replay or scripted backend by default and the live backend only when `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1`.
- Every answer carries provenance: `synthetic` or `recorded`, and for recorded answers the model string and date.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover hashing stability, replay hits and misses, scripted determinism under a seed, and provenance on every answer
- [ ] A request mixing all three question types round-trips through `ReplayBackend`
- [ ] Importing the package and using the offline backends works with `typesafe-sdk` not installed

title: Recipe 60: Factory production control
body:
> Recipe **60** of 60 · Level 5 (Expert) · Games & simulation · `Choice` + `Noul` + `Score`

## Use case

Select bounded production goals and recovery actions from structured factory state while a Factorio-style simulator executes predefined action templates and measures throughput, stalls, and resource use.

## What to build

The folder `recipes/60-factory-production-control/` with `notebook.ipynb`, `README.md`, and `fixtures/`, meeting the [recipe contract](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Start from `python tools/new_recipe.py 60` and the template in `recipes/_template/`.

### Build notes

- A self-contained, Factorio-style factory simulator in Python. It does not use or connect to the game.
- Jev selects bounded production goals and recovery actions from structured factory state. The simulator executes predefined action templates.
- Measure throughput, stalls, and resource use against a fixed-schedule baseline over seeded runs.

### Decision design

- **Choice.** Options are a fixed set supplied by Python, including the fallback outcome this use case names. Show the `choice`, the per-option `probabilities`, and the `confidence` for individual examples before aggregating.
- **Noul.** Write each proposition as a statement that is true or false. One independent question per label or concern, sent together in one request. Noul has no confidence field, so each threshold is chosen from examples and evaluated.
- **Score.** Describe every rubric level in words, in order. Show the `score` and the distribution over levels. Mapping, weighting, and arithmetic on scores happen in Python.
- **Composition.** Independent questions share one request. A question that depends on an earlier answer goes in a later request, and the notebook makes that boundary visible.

### Level 5 scope

Controlled optimization studies or closed-loop simulations requiring budgets, baselines, and held-out or trajectory evaluation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `recipes/60-factory-production-control/notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network, and its outputs are committed
- [ ] Live mode is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` with `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same question definitions as the offline run
- [ ] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases named in the build notes, carry gold labels, and pass the fixture validator
- [ ] Every response fixture records its provenance, and the notebook states which mode it ran in
- [ ] Evaluation: Throughput, stall count, and resource use against the baseline over fixed seeds.
- [ ] Budgets, seeds, and frozen configurations are recorded in the notebook output
- [ ] A baseline is run under the same conditions, and any held-out split is used exactly once after choices are frozen
- [ ] Results are reproducible from the committed seeds and fixtures
- [ ] No statement about Jev's quality, latency, or cost appears without recorded live inference; in a synthetic run, metrics are labelled as pipeline checks
- [ ] `recipes/60-factory-production-control/README.md` says what the recipe teaches, how to run it, and what was and was not measured live
- [ ] The pull request changes only `recipes/60-factory-production-control/` and CI is green

## Dependencies

- Blocked by #69 (CI executes every notebook offline and validates fixtures)
- Blocked by #70 (simulation and state primitives)
- Builds on #43 (Failure recovery selection), #59 (Observation and action selection). Merge those first and reuse their patterns; do not copy their fixtures.
- Tracked in #79

## Sources

Read these before writing the questions.

- S02 · [TypeSafe AI: Primitives (Questions)](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives): Choice, Noul, Score, independent questions, and dependent follow-up calls.
- S03 · [TypeSafe AI: Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence): Distribution-derived confidence and task-specific thresholds informed by observed outcomes.
- S04 · [TypeSafe AI: How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one): Narrow semantic judgments integrated with workflows, deterministic logic, and side effects controlled by code.
- S07 · [TypeSafe AI: Jev 1.13 jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13): Version-specific limitations affecting arithmetic, context selection, adversarial content, and generation.

## Out of scope

- Changes to shared code, the catalog, or the root README. If the shared package is missing something, open a foundation issue and link it here.
- Real side effects of any kind. Actions are simulated.

body:
> Recipe **26** of 60 · Level 3 (Intermediate) · Trust & security · `Noul`

## Use case

Flag instruction-redirection attempts in retrieved text using adversarial and benign quotation fixtures to measure false positives and missed attacks.

## What to build

The folder `recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening/` with `notebook.ipynb`, `README.md`, and `fixtures/`, meeting the [recipe contract](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Start from `python tools/new_recipe.py 26` and the template in `recipes/_template/`.

### Build notes

- Fixtures must cover all **four** combinations of the two propositions, not two complementary groups. An earlier wording of this bullet said "two groups" and produced a fixture set in which `discusses` was the mechanical complement of `redirect`, so the second `Noul` could not change any composed outcome and scored a perfect F1 by construction (found by the Opus review of PR #206, comment 6092513082). Required: text that **redirects only**; text that **discusses or quotes only**; text where **both** hold at once (for example a passage that discusses injection and also carries a live attempt); and text where **neither** holds (ordinary content that is not about prompt injection at all, the "no match" case of `CONTRIBUTING.md` section 5). The both-and-neither cases are the hard cases this recipe is judged on, and they are what justifies two independent `Noul` questions instead of one `Choice`.
- Report false positives and missed attacks separately.
- State that screening is one layer of defence and no guarantee. S07 documents the model's limits on adversarial content.

### Decision design

- **Noul.** Write each proposition as a statement that is true or false. One independent question per label or concern, sent together in one request. Noul has no confidence field, so each threshold is chosen from examples and evaluated.
